title: 3 Things Off-Plan Buyers Never Check: Windows, Street and Floor
seoTitle: 3 Things Off-Plan Buyers Never Check Before Signing
description: Most presale buyers sign for a unit they never really saw. Check which way your windows face, what is across the street, and which floor you are buying.
answer: Before you sign for an off-plan unit, check three details the brochure does not show you: which way your windows face, what is across the street today and what could be built there in a few years, and the actual floor you are buying. The brochure sells the whole building, but you are only buying one unit.
keywords: what to check before buying off-plan
body:
Most people who buy a presale apartment sign for a home they never really saw. They saw the building. They saw the lobby, the pool and the penthouse views in the renderings. But the unit they bought is one specific box in that tower, and three details about that box decide how it will feel to live in and how easy it will be to sell.

## Why the brochure is not your unit

A brochure is made to sell the whole project. It shows the best angle, the best view and the best floor. That is normal marketing. The problem is that buyers let that picture stand in for their own unit. You are not buying the building. You are buying one unit, and you need to look at that unit on its own.

## The 3 details to check before you sign

1. **Which way your windows face.** A north-facing unit and a south-facing unit in the same tower are two different homes. Light, heat and view all change with orientation. Ask for the floor plan with the compass direction marked, and know exactly where your windows point.
2. **What is across the street.** Look at what sits in front of your windows today, and then ask what could be there in three years. A park or an empty lot today can become another tower tomorrow. If your view is the reason you are paying more, find out whether that view is protected.
3. **Your actual floor.** The renderings usually show the view from the penthouse. If you are buying on the 8th floor, your view is the 8th floor view. Ask what can be seen from your height, not from the top of the building.

## A simple way to use this checklist

Before you sign, write down three answers next to your unit number: the direction of your windows, what is across the street now and what is planned there, and the floor you are on. If the sales team cannot answer any of these clearly, keep asking until they can. These are basic facts about the product you are paying for.

## Why these details matter later

Orientation, view and floor are among the things that shape how a unit feels day to day and how it compares with others in the same building. In my experience, they are also the details buyers notice only after they move in, when it is too late to choose a different unit. Checking them takes a few questions now and can save you years of regret.
takeaways: Most presale buyers sign for a unit they never really saw.
North-facing and south-facing units in the same tower are two different homes.
What is across the street today may not be there in three years.
Renderings show the penthouse view, not the view from your floor.
The brochure sells the building, but you are buying one unit.
faq: What should I check before buying an off-plan apartment?
Check which way your windows face, what is across the street now and what could be built there later, and the actual floor of your unit, not just the building as shown in the brochure.
Does window orientation matter when buying a condo?
Yes. North-facing and south-facing units in the same building get different light, heat and views, so they can feel like two different homes.
Can the view from my presale unit change after I buy?
It can. An open lot or a park across the street today could become another building in a few years, so ask what is planned there before you sign.
Do off-plan renderings show my actual view?
Usually not. Renderings often show the view from the top floors, so ask what can actually be seen from the floor you are buying.
